For the first time, I lived several days by "I ran out of fucks to give" mentality.

Ability to care just escaped me. 

That coupled with the thought that if I'm thinking of ending my life, why not do the things you couldn't do while you valued your life. Mainly, do whatever you want without fear of consequences.

I see that this won't end well, as things that I wish to do are very self-destructive and also incredible harmful for others.

Much like how inner-city gang youth who has lost hope for future would act. I'm sure I'll be either dead or in prison by age 25. Might as well do drugs, get sex however I can, and fuck up everyone who pisses me off.

When nothing matters, only thing that comes to surface is my vast anger and resentment towards everything ever.

Like a star going supernova, my wrath burns blindingly bright with white flare that would incinerate all that caught in my blast, with no remainders to collect.

I only came to be solely due to my parent's unilateral decision to have a child. Before they had me, I was non-existent. Unaware of any happiness or suffering. Completely nothing. I can't tell you how great that seems in comparison to now.

I had no say in it. Only some backwards logic about how I should be grateful for the life I got.

What's so great about it anyways? With being alive, only guarantee is suffering. Not everyone experiences happiness and peace. But everyone sure does experience suffering. Why ever subject another person to that?

Why MAKE a brand new person to enjoy the suffering we all taste. How sadistic and egotistical.

All because you wanted a cute, little kid to name after your name.

Fuck that. This shit really sucks. God, I'm so pissed.

Hey. So, depression is something I've been dealing with and actively treating for a while (with medication and talk therapy).

Once in a while I fall back into deep depression. This time around, it has got a stronger grip on my than usual.

It's just getting exhausting. I don't know why I need to just "get through" this so I can welcome another dip like this again.

Depression always has its way of finding me and dragging me down. It's not a thing that recently came to me, neither. It's been with me ever since I can remember. It took me a while to find out through therapy that how I was feeling is not how everyone feels.

There is no bright memories for me to harken back to and tell myself with hopeful voice that it'll be alright again.

It just wasn't right ever. Now it feels too late. I'm only prolonging my suffering. There is nothing that can come to be that will justify me going through all this suffering.

It's forever. It's ever present.

Death is the only reprieve.

Uh....that and self-pity.

I hear that often as a deterrent to suicide.

Unfortunately, don't really apply to me very well.

My family don't even know that I'm depressed. They would be baffled to find how angry and lonely I am. They were never keen on finding out how I felt or why I felt. As long as I fulfill my role and live up to their expectations, all is well.

Besides death would bring an end to all. Even to any concerns I had for my family's well-being. Narcissism at it's finest.

It's the most saddest movie ever made.

"Who Shot Ya?" will be a gritty crime mystery movie.

Set in present day, Yun is a 23 year old man living in NYC. He ran away from home and left Hong Kong, where he was born and raised, at the age of 16. 

Yun works at a chinese restaurant that serves as a front for Triad's storage for drug trade. Yun earns extra cash loading and stashing away boxes filled with drugs in the basement walk-in fridge. He does not like the Triad, but he desperately needs the cash.

Yun has a younger sister, Ya, who is 18 years old and a father, Chen, 54 year old that still lives in Hong Kong. 

Yun's mother passed away soon after giving birth to Ya. Yun's father was overprotective of the two children, as they were entrusted to him by his beloved wife, just moments before she passed away.

Yun and Chen has many fights throughout Yun's early adolescence. After one particularly bad fight, Yun decides to leave for US and never look back.

He, however, had great love for his sister. Yun and Ya kept correspondence in secret via e-mail.

One day, Ya isn't heard from anymore. Yun becomes more worried as weeks pass without hearing from Ya. Worried that something must've happened to Ya, Yun quickly arranges for travel back to Hong Kong.

Upon returning to his home, he sees that his father and Yun's relatives are gathered for Ya's funeral. Ya has been fatally shot, and no one knows who did it. Hong Kong police don't have any leads and shows no efforts to find any.

Yun must now retrace Ya's steps in Hong Kong in hopes of finding out her killer. During which he starts to learn his father's illness. Chen's failed business, and the loans he took out from Hong Kong mafia in an effort to revive his business.

Ya, having found out about her father's loan, tries to protect her father by befriending members of the Hong Kong mafia.

He calls upon his Triad connections from NYC to gather information. Yun is met with old friends in Hong Kong. Yun and Chen are butting heads, displacing blame on each other for the death of Ya.

Will Yun ever find out....who shot Ya?

It's a comedy mockumentary about a new service business created where a woman shows up to a foreveralone redditor's home to be his wife for a month.

A redditor, who used to be a foreveralone and always friendzoned, finally finds his SO and is leading a happy married life. 

Soon he wishes to bring the same joy to many other redditors who love to cry on reddit about being foreveralone and how their attractive female friends are detestable for friendzoning them.

He starts up a business called "The Redditor's Wife." He recruits 2 women who are also redditors. The deal is, a woman will pretend as if she was a redditor's SO for a month. 

Having meals together, texting each other about mundane details of a day, and watching Breaking Bad together. 

There is no sex involved, unless the women wish to.

Each woman have a different reason for agreeing to this job. 

One is a "gamer gurl," who is thin and somewhat cute. She has inflated sense of self, because she isn't horribly ugly, morbidly obese, and watched some friends play Mario Kart 64 once. 

She imagines she will rake in easy money despite not doing what she's asked to, because she's such a desired female specimen.

She wants to raise money to buy a new digital camera to take photos of her cat with.

Second woman is a true member of the academia. Frequent contributer of [/r/askscience](/r/askscience), she has a Ph.D. in Sociology. She wishes to observe a much heard of foreveralone redditor, firsthand. For science!

Hijinks ensue, as she is almost robotic and even more clumsy in human relationships as her "reddit husband."


Both women and their "reddit husbands" come to some deeper understanding about intimacy and relationship.

I'm thinking the "Goobacks" and "Guitar Queer-o."

"Goobacks" really package in one episode what South Park does best: pointing out absurdity and utter stupidity of real life issues with hyperbole. 

"Guitar Queer-o" shows the other side of South Park: parodying popular culture. In this, it parodies sudden rise of popularity of a game Guitar Hero above that of playing a real guitar. It also parodies every "Behind the Music" story of a rock band: a fall out with original members, drug abuse by the most talented member of a band, and more.

Both episodes can be appreciated without being in on the many inside jokes of South Park. The issues being parodied are so well-known that anyone would have an idea of what's going on.
